briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for October 31, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis: A Health and Economic Emergency
sections.content: Shocking news has emerged that 3 million people have died due to heatwaves, pushing global health into an emergency phase [1]. Beyond these direct human casualties, delaying climate crisis response could significantly destabilize Gross Domestic Product (GDP), and a massive economic bill is anticipated for achieving carbon neutrality [9]. Furthermore, voices are emerging, such as 'We cannot condone meat-grilling festivals in an era of climate crisis,' indicating that the climate crisis is influencing daily life and culture, urging a shift in public perception [5]. This clearly demonstrates that the climate crisis is no longer a distant future problem, but an immediate emergency impacting health, economy, and society as a whole.

sections.title: 🌍 International Biodiversity Negotiations: Expectations and Challenges
sections.content: The COP17 UN Biodiversity Conference, held in Yerevan, Armenia, has concluded, resulting in a 'fragile agreement' to enhance nature conservation and financial support [24]. Nations have completed their first 'global review' of progress towards reversing nature loss by 2030 [26], but simultaneously, growing concerns suggest that countries are expected to fail in meeting their nature targets [25]. Notably, criticism is mounting that the convention will continue its 34-year history of never achieving its targets, leading to increased calls for COP summit reforms [25]. This indicates that the international community's efforts in nature protection continue to face significant barriers to realistic implementation.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts Expand and Capacity Building Strengthens
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts to achieve carbon neutrality are spreading across local governments and civil society. In Incheon, carbon neutrality practices are spreading among citizens, with next year's action plan being concretized [11], and Yeonggwang County has presented a model regional case by winning an 'Excellence Award' in the carbon neutrality outstanding city/county evaluation [13]. Asan City Council's Special Committee on Carbon Neutrality is working on discovering region-specific policies and preparing a 180-day action plan through expert lectures and capacity-building training for its members [7, 8, 12, 14, 15], and Cheongju City, Chungcheongbuk-do, has also conducted carbon neutrality capacity-building training for all its employees [16]. Furthermore, concrete energy transition movements are observed, such as Gokseong County signing an RE100 regulatory innovation agreement to attract renewable energy-based companies [17].

sections.title: 📰 Climate Change Discourse and Scientific Insights
sections.content: Academic and policy discussions on climate change continue to deepen. The achievements of William Nordhaus, a Nobel laureate for his work integrating economics and climate change, have been re-examined [20], and Bjorn Lomborg has presented diverse perspectives on climate discourse, stating that climate change should be viewed as a 'problem' rather than the 'end of the world' [21]. Meanwhile, an international review has revealed the importance of hidden Arctic root processes in climate change, broadening scientific understanding [22]. London Mayor Khan emphasized that cities can both contribute to and offer solutions for climate change, presenting a new perspective on the role of urban areas [23]. These discussions demonstrate the need for a multifaceted approach and a profound understanding of the climate change issue.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the severity of the climate crisis, alongside the convergence of various domestic and international response efforts. This is a moment that demands stronger and more tangible actions for the survival of humanity and a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
